# eBay

2 endpoints, all GET. Base URL `https://www.socialcrawl.dev`, auth header `x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY`.

**Credit costs:** 2 advanced (5) - the exact cost is in each endpoint heading below.

| [GET /v1/ebay/search](#get-v1ebaysearch---5-credits-advanced) | 5 credits (advanced) | Returns eBay listings with item ID, price, seller rating, and units sold… | Use it to scan active or ended marketplace listings, then pull full detail by item id… |

eBay listing data. Single-item detail and keyword search, on the canonical Product schema shared with the other retail platforms.

<!-- BEGIN:GENERATED:ENDPOINTS (auto-generated by generate-docs.ts - AIP-16b) -->

## GET /v1/ebay/product - 5 credits (advanced)

Returns full detail for a single eBay listing: title, brand, price, original price, currency, condition and condition notes, MPN and UPC, units available, units sold, watchers, and the seller. The seller block is the reason to call this rather than search: product.ext.seller_reputation carries lifetime feedback percentage and count, top-rated status, items sold, join date, and four detailed sub-ratings for description accuracy, shipping cost, shipping speed, and communication. One known gap: eBay's detail response currently returns a corrupt image array, so image_urls is null here. Use the image on the matching GET /v1/ebay/search row, which is unaffected.

**Use when** the seller matters as much as the item: it carries feedback score, top-rated status, join date, and four detailed sub-ratings.
**Cost** cache 600 s
**Paging** none

**Query params**

- `product_id` (required) - eBay item id, the numeric id in a listing URL: ebay.com/itm/327256602116 is item id 327256602116. Item ids also come back on every row of GET /v1/ebay/search. · e.g. `327256602116`
- `country` (optional, enum: US | GB | AU | CA | DE | FR | IT | ES | IE | AT | CH | NL | BE | PL | SG | MY | PH | HK | MX) - eBay marketplace as a two-letter country code: US (ebay.com, default), GB, AU, CA, DE, FR, IT, ES, IE, AT, CH, NL, BE, PL, SG, MY, PH, HK, or MX. The marketplace sets the listing pool, language, and currency.

**Response** `Product` object at `data`, `{ product }` ([full schema](schemas/Product.md))

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `product.title` | Product title |
| `product.id` | Platform product ID… |
| `product.brand` | Brand name (cleaned). |
| `product.description` |  |
| `product.seller` |  |
| `product.price.currency` |  |

+2 more (types in the full schema): `product.price` {current, original}. Also in the sample: `product` {url string, image_urls null, availability null, reviews_count null}; `product.rating` {average null, count null}; `product.ext` {sold_count number, condition string, available_quantity number}; `product.ext.seller_reputation` {feedback_percentage number, feedback_count number, top_rated boolean, items_sold number, joined string, url string}; `product.ext.seller_reputation.detailed_ratings` {accurate_description number, reasonable_shipping_cost number} (+2 more).

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/ebay/product" \
  --data-urlencode "product_id=327256602116" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/ebay/search - 5 credits (advanced)

Returns eBay listings matching a keyword, 60 per page on an active search, each with its item id, title, price, original price where the listing is discounted, currency, condition, image, seller handle, seller feedback percentage and count, units sold, buying format, and the listing URL. completed_items returns ended listings, and free_shipping restricts results to listings with free delivery. sold_items is temporarily rejected before billing because the upstream now requires a private eBay session cookie, which SocialCrawl does not accept or forward. Feed a returned item id into GET /v1/ebay/product for the full listing including seller reputation depth. When crawling, note that the result total eBay reports is an estimate that changes between pages, so it is not returned here: paginate until a page comes back empty.

**Use when** you want to scan active or ended marketplace listings, then pull full detail by item id. Sold-comps search is temporarily unavailable.
**Cost** cache 120 s
**Paging** page (native `page`) · ≈60/page (observed once) · depth unknown · N items ≈ ceil(N/60) x 5 credits

**Query params**

- `query` (required) - Free-text listing search, for example airpods pro or vintage seiko. · e.g. `airpods pro`
- `country` (optional, enum: US | GB | AU | CA | DE | FR | IT | ES | IE | AT | CH | NL | BE | PL | SG | MY | PH | HK | MX) - eBay marketplace as a two-letter country code: US (ebay.com, default), GB, AU, CA, DE, FR, IT, ES, IE, AT, CH, NL, BE, PL, SG, MY, PH, HK, or MX. The marketplace sets the listing pool, language, and currency.
- `page` (optional, integer, 1-100) - Page number, starting at 1. Prefer the universal cursor parameter.
- `sort_by` (optional, enum: best_match | price_low | price_high | newly_listed | ending_soonest) - Result ordering: best_match (default), price_low, price_high, newly_listed, or ending_soonest.
- `condition` (optional, enum: new | refurbished | used) - Restrict to one item condition: new, refurbished, or used.
- `buying_format` (optional, enum: auction | buy_it_now | accepts_offers) - Restrict to one sale type: auction, buy_it_now, or accepts_offers.
- `show_only` (optional, string) - Restrict results with completed_items or free_shipping; combine supported values with a comma. sold_items is temporarily unavailable and is rejected before billing because the upstream requires a private eBay session cookie. SocialCrawl does not accept or forward session cookies.
- `min_price` (optional, string) - Lowest price to include. Applied by eBay and approximate, so filter on product.price.current if you need a hard bound.
- `max_price` (optional, string) - Highest price to include. Applied by eBay and approximate, so filter on product.price.current if you need a hard bound.
- `aspects` (optional, string) - Category-specific item aspect filter taken from a previous response, for example Brand:Apple.

**Response** `ProductList` rows at `data.items[]`, each `{ product }` ([full schema](schemas/ProductList.md))

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `product.id` | Platform product ID… |
| `product.title` | Product title |
| `product.url` | Direct URL to the product page |
| `product.image_urls` | Primary image URL, or an array of image URLs for products… |
| `product.reviews_count` |  |
| `product.seller` |  |

+5 more (types in the full schema): `product.price` {currency, current, original}; `product.rating` {average, count}. Also in the sample: `product` {description null, brand null, availability null}; `product.ext` {sold_count number, condition string, buying_format string}; `product.ext.seller_reputation` {feedback_percentage number, feedback_count number, top_rated boolean, items_sold null, joined null, url null, detailed_ratings null}. Page-level: `data.dropped`.

**Next** `ebay/product` (`product_id` ← `data.items[].product.id`) - Get an eBay listing by item id.

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/ebay/search" \
  --data-urlencode "query=airpods pro" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```
